text: Which format change is the one no automated check can detect?
choices: Reordering two columns while keeping their names unchanged.
Removing a column that no current reader consults.
Changing the meaning of an existing field — publication year becoming acquisition year, without a rename.
Adding a new column at the end of a CSV file that has a header.
explanation: The data parses perfectly and is wrong. Adding is safe with header-driven readers; removing and reordering break loudly enough to be caught. A change of meaning produces plausible values of the right type in the right place — which is why the rule is to add a new field and deprecate the old one rather than repurpose, and why a version number in the file is worth its two lines.
